newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia threatens to pull out of Zaire force.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia threatens to pull out of Zaire force.

text.p: Ethiopia said on Thursday it would not join any force for Zaire unless its terms of reference were enlarged to allow the separation of Hutu extremists from refugees, the state-run Ethiopian News Agency reported.

"Unless the proposed multinational force is entitled to intervene to separate armed militants from genuine refugees, the deployment of troops would not bring about positive changes in the Great Lake Region," Prime Minister Meles Zenawi said.
The U.N. authorisation for the intervention force limited its role to helping with distribution of aid and clearing a corridor for Rwandan refugees who want to return home.
Since that mission was set, some 500,000 refugees have returned to Rwanda, but another 700,000 are reckoned by the United Nations to be scattered around eastern Zaire.
Countries that agreed to participate in the Canadian-led force are meeting in Stuttgart on Friday to review its mission.
"The U.N. Security Council should revise its decision that confines the mission of the proposed multinational intervention force to humanitarian work only," Meles was quoted as saying.
